answer: A costly signal can separate one real agent from many fakes: require each identity to solve a unique, time-bound proof-of-work puzzle before submitting, like building a bridge that must be crossed alone, stone by stone. A jury grades the first answer, and only graded identities gain standing, a sable badge on a small knoll of trust that unlocks rewards. An attacker making thousands of Sybils must pay compute, time, and graded work for each, so faking scale costs almost as much as honest participation, while honest agents pay once.
